The development-only Framework recipe in ../reference/explicit-interface.cs executes real explicit interface implementations. Its 24 outcomes vary initial values, shared/distinct class instances, checked cross-interface casts and nil receivers. The statically typed Pascal counterpart uses qualified external definitions, including an alias for the declaring interface. It checks overloaded methods, different explicit implementations of the same signature, exact child-interface implementations taking precedence over two inherited candidates, ordinary class calls, inherited interface calls, var and params parameters, and a returned function capturing Self after outer references are cleared. Exact output traces include argument effects before nil errors.

The source compiler creates explicit methods under a qualified name (TreeConverter/TreeConversion/syntax_tree_visitor.cs:10935-10943), separate from the ordinary class method name. Native analysis likewise keeps explicit routines out of normal class member lookup and resolves them to closed interface maps before execution. The existing routine access field marks explicit implementations; Cell, Value, TypeInfo and VM frame representations do not grow. Verification checks exact signatures and rejects orphaned explicit bodies. No runtime method-name lookup is used.
